Operator: Good day, and welcome to the AmpliNet Communications Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question at that time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. If you're using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset to allow optimal sound quality. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the call over to Jordan Lee, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Jordan Lee: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to AmpliNet Communications' Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Emma Rodriguez, Chief Executive Officer; Kevin Patel, Chief Financial Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Network Officer; Tyler Brooks, Chief Commercial Officer; Nina Patel, Chief Technology Officer; Carlos Mendoza, Chief Operating Officer; and other members of our leadership team. Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Emma Rodriguez: Thank you, Jordan, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q2, demonstrating our continued commitment to growth and innovation. Our success is driven by our dedicated team and strategic investments. Our key achievements include significant progress in network investments, particularly our 5G deployment and capital expenditures, which form the foundation of our long-term strategy. We've also seen positive ARPU trends influenced by our pricing and bundling approaches. Service revenues across wireless, broadband, and enterprise segments showed solid growth. We've managed cost of revenue effectively, analyzed churn trends closely, advanced enterprise and B2B initiatives with notable wins, expanded our fiber buildout with impressive coverage and adoption, and generated strong free cash flow for strategic deployment.

The launch of AmpliStream Ultra is exceeding expectations, resulting in heightened subscriber engagement and media revenue uplift. Further milestones include accelerating our 5G standalone architecture and fiber expansions. We are also focusing on enterprise private networks and cybersecurity enhancements. Our dedication to customer retention through loyalty programs is bearing fruit. Our strategy is to enhance converged bundling for higher lifetime value. We are actively investing in edge computing and AI-driven optimizations. We are also exploring international JVs for spectrum sharing and finally, analyzing sustainability in our deployments to reduce energy use.

Kevin Patel: Thank you, Emma. Now, let's review our financial performance. Revenue for the quarter reached $29.5 billion, reflecting a 7% increase year-over-year. Adjusted EBITDA was $10.2 billion, resulting in a margin of 34.6%. We maintain a disciplined approach to cost management and capital allocation. Capital expenditures totaled $2.8 billion, primarily allocated to expanding our 5G network, fiber infrastructure, and content investments.

Good morning again, everyone. As your CFO, I'd like to dive deeper into our network investments, where 5G deployment progress and capital expenditures stand as the cornerstone of our strategy at AmpliNet Communications. As a leading integrated telecom and media player, we're building one of the fastest 5G networks, leveraging it for premium connectivity, enterprise solutions, and superior media experiences that set us apart from competitors like Verizon or T-Mobile.

On capex, Q2 saw $2.8 billion deployed, up 12% year-over-year and aligned with full-year guidance of $10.5 to $11.5 billion. About 65%, or $1.8 billion, went to 5G, including radio access network upgrades, backhaul densification, and core evolution—an 8% increase reflecting efficiencies from Open RAN pilots with Nokia and Samsung, cutting site costs by 15%. RAN took $1.2 billion, focused on sub-6GHz massive MIMO on C-band spectrum from the 2021 FCC auction. Backhaul and transport used $400 million for 400G fiber upgrades supporting over 10 Tbps throughput in key markets. The rest funded edge computing and 5G fixed wireless access, enhancing low-latency streaming for our AmpliStream platform.

Deployment-wise, we're ahead: 88% nationwide 5G coverage for 280 million Americans, beating our 85% year-end 2023 goal. This covers 55,000 upgraded sites, 70% NSA and 30% SA, enabling URLLC for IoT and eMBB at 450 Mbps median downloads. Northeast at 96%, with mmWave in NYC and Boston hitting 3 Gbps peaks, driving 22% ARPU from 5G Ultra bundles with ad-free AmpliStream. Midwest and Southeast at 82% and 85%, prioritizing sub-6GHz rural reach via Crown Castle small cells. Our European JV with Vodafone in UK and Germany reached 75% coverage for 50 million pops, sharing 3.5 GHz spectrum and saving 20% capex.

We've pushed tech boundaries: SA core in 15 MSAs for slicing, signing 12 enterprise deals like Ford for vehicles and a studio for virtual production. Open RAN at 2,500 sites with Ericsson Cloud RAN and DISH virtualization cuts opex 18%. Sustainability: 40% new sites with AI power management, down 25% energy use.

Returns are strong: 5G subs at 62% of mobile base from 45%, +9% service revenue. Edge CDN $150 million slashed streaming latency 40ms, +15% AmpliStream engagement. FWA to 2 million homes by year-end, 35% take rates in pilots.

Q3 capex $2.7-2.9 billion, front-loading SA. Supply issues add 5-7%, but multi-vendor and CHIPS Act help. This gains us 200 bps postpaid share by 2025.

Turning to ARPU trends, we hit blended postpaid ARPU of $58.42, +5.8% YoY from $55.21—a $3.21 gain from pricing, bundling, and premium services. Full-year $57.18, +4.9%, beating peers amid OTT pressure.

Mobile postpaid $48.76, +4.2% YoY, from 5G Ultra plans at 28% penetration, +100GB hotspot, roaming. 3-5% hikes on mid-tier, SA for AR/cloud adding $0.50. Fixed broadband $72.34, +7.1%, FTTH 45% footprint, gigabit premiums, 62% 'AmpliNet Total Home' bundles +18% ARPU. Video/media $32.18, +3.4%, AmpliFlex at $25 with Peacock/Max, +22% attach to 41%.

US $61.50 +6.2%, Europe €48.20 +3.1%, APAC/LATAM $42.80 +5.5%. Convergence lowers churn 20%, +25% LTV. FY24 4-6% growth, AI pricing pilots.

Service revenue hit $14.2 billion, +7.8% reported, 8.2% constant currency—11th straight quarter up. Wireless $8.9 billion +5.2%, 312k postpaid adds, ARPU $56.42 +2.3%, 42% Unlimited Max, 5G SA 85% coverage, 450 Mbps. Prepaid +1.8%, Open RAN rural. Northeast/Sunbelt 70% adds, LATAM JV +12%.

Broadband $3.4 billion +9.7%, 178k FWA/245k FTTH adds, 12.8M subs +14%, ARPU $68.20 +3.1%, 60% gigabit+, 28k route miles fiber, FWA 2.5M. Southeast +22%, UK +7%. Enterprise $2.0 billion +12.4%, mobile +15% slicing with Ford/P&G, fixed +10% dark fiber/AWS. $250M hospital 5G, IoT 3.2M +28%, ARPU $1,250 +4.2%. NA 75%, APAC +20%.

FY service 7-8%, margins +120 bps to 42.1%.

Cost of revenue $12.4 billion +4% YoY, flat QoQ, 42.3% of revenue—110 bps better. Network $7.2B 58% +3% despite 25% traffic, Open RAN 15% sites -18% TCO, vRAN -12% opex. US spectrum efficiency +30%, Europe AI maintenance -15% energy. Content $2.7B +12% sports, but revenue-share $180M save. Devices $1.5B +6%, $350/sub, vendor financing. Q3 $12.6-12.8B, 40-41%, edge nodes 25% savings, EU interconnect saves.

Churn blended postpaid 0.92%, -10 bps QoQ, -13 bps YoY—best in years, below AT&T/Verizon. Postpaid mobility 0.85% -15 bps YoY, loyalty AI -22% voluntary, but involuntary +3 bps credit. US 0.78%, Europe 1.02%. Broadband 1.12% -10 bps, FTTH 0.65%, bundles +18 NPS. Video 2.15% -35 bps, AI recs +15%. Saved $175M, Q4 sub-0.90%.

Enterprise/B2B $2.8B +28%, 32% service rev, margins +450 bps 42%. 5G private 45 customers +60%, IoT 4.2M +35% ARPU $145. SD-WAN $1.2B ARR +55%. CDN $450M +22%. Wins: $650M Siemens-like manufacturing, $420M JPM-like SASE, $380M AWS edge, $250M Netflix CDN. TCV $2.5B. NA +32%, EMEA +24%, APAC +45%. FY 27%, pipeline $15B.

Fiber: 4,200 route miles Q2 +28% seq, YTD 7,800 +12%. Cost/mile $52k -15%, XGS-PON 85%. Passed 8.2M homes/businesses +22% YoY, +1.1M seq: Sunbelt 2.4M +280k, Northeast 1.9M +150k, rural +220k RDOF/BEAD. Subs 2.85M +420k, take 34.8% +500 bps, ARPU $118, 62% 1Gig+, bundles 78%. SMB 285k. Q3 700k passed, 450k adds. Revenue $785M 68% margin.

Full-year FCF $12.8B +18%, OCF $30.7B +12%, capex $17.9B. Utilization: $7B shareholder (div $4.2B, buyback $2.8B), debt $3.2B leverage 2.1x, growth $1.9B, cash $700M. 2024 $13.5-14B.

Maria Gonzalez: Thank you, Kevin. I'm pleased to provide an update on our network advancements. We've significantly expanded our 5G coverage to 88% nationwide, delivering faster speeds averaging 450 Mbps and lower latency under 10ms in SA markets. Reliability is at 99.999%, with ongoing optimizations for surging data demand. Cybersecurity enhancements include AI threat detection across our edge sites. We remain committed to sustainable deployments, with 40% of sites featuring power-saving tech.

Tyler Brooks: Thank you. I'm excited to share our commercial achievements. Strong subscriber growth: 312k postpaid wireless, 423k broadband, enterprise momentum. Satisfaction high, NPS up 18 points from bundles. Partnerships expanding for converged services like AmpliStream with Peacock. Prioritizing low churn at 0.92% blended through loyalty.

Nina Patel: Thank you. From a technology perspective, we're driving innovation with AI and ML for network automation, customer service bots, and new services like AR/VR streaming. R&D investments keep us ahead, including Open RAN scaling and 50G PON pilots. Our direction emphasizes AI-native networks and edge for GenAI.

Carlos Mendoza: Thank you. Operationally, efficiency gains from data analytics optimize resources. Sustainability efforts cut energy 15%, with green builds. Focus on streamlining for 42.5% OCF margins.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from John Smith with Morningstar. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more details on your content strategy and your plans for investing in original programming, and what is the anticipated impact on subscriber growth?

Emma Rodriguez: Thanks, John. Our content strategy centers on converged bundles like AmpliFlex, integrating Peacock, Paramount+, and Max with our 5G home internet and originals from AmpliStream. We're investing $500 million annually in originals, focusing on live sports and AR/VR exclusives, leveraging edge CDN for 40ms lower latency. This has driven video attach to 41%, +22% YoY, with 15% engagement lift on AmpliStream during events. Expect 18% sub growth in FY24, offsetting cord-cutting via skinny bundles and 85% retention.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your plans for addressing the digital divide and ensuring that all communities have access to affordable broadband, and how do you plan to achieve nationwide coverage goals?

Tyler Brooks: Great question, Lisa. We're tackling the digital divide through FWA rollout to 2 million underserved homes by year-end, 35% take rates, and fiber rural push with $1.2B RDOF/$850M BEAD, adding 220k homes Q2. Affordable plans at $50/month unlimited, bundled with education zero-rating. Nationwide coverage via 88% 5G, FTTH 8.2M passed targeting 10M by 2025, hybrid Starlink backhaul. This closes gaps in Midwest/Southeast, aiming 95% high-speed access by 2026.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Johnson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson: Can you discuss your capital allocation priorities and your plans for returning capital to shareholders, including buybacks and dividends?

Kevin Patel: Thanks, Mike. Balanced allocation: 55% FCF to shareholders—$4.2B dividends at 45-50% payout, 4.8% yield; $2.8B buybacks under $15B program, retiring 4.1% shares, +6% EPS. 25% debt reduction to 2.1x leverage, 15% growth like spectrum/M&A, 5% cash. FY24 FCF $13.5-14B supports this, prioritizing deleveraging then returns amid 5G ROI.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Sarah Lee: What are your strategies for navigating the changing regulatory landscape?

Emma Rodriguez: Thanks, Sarah. We're proactive: EU Gigabit targets aid fiber JVs, CHIPS Act boosts domestic RAN, BEAD/RDOF $2B+ funds rural. Monitoring C-band refills, DMA interconnect cuts. Compliance via data sovereignty edges, lobbying for spectrum harmony. Multi-vendor de-risks Huawei bans, positioning for 200 bps share gains.

Jordan Lee: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Emma, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Emma Rodriguez: Thank you. In conclusion, we are pleased with our performance this quarter and remain confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We are committed to innovation, customer satisfaction, and sustainability. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
